chunks: Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the ghusl of the deceased: how should he be washed? He said: “With water and sidr, and wash his whole body; then wash him again with water and camphor; then wash him again with water.” I said: “Three times?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Then what should be upon him when one washes him?” He said: “If you are able for a shirt to be upon him, then wash him from beneath the shirt.”

key_terms.سِدْرٍ: lote leaves used in the first washing of the body
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.قَمِيصٌ: a shirt covering the deceased during washing
key_terms.كَافُورٍ: camphor used in the second washing of the deceased
key_terms.مِنْ تَحْتِ الْقَمِيصِ: washing from beneath the shirt to preserve covering

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be washed in Shia fiqh according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the prescribed method of ghusl for the deceased: first with water and sidr, then with water and camphor, and then with plain water, making three washings in total. It also instructs that, if possible, the deceased should have a shirt on while being washed, and the washing should be done from beneath it.
